intro: The ritual of Zelliya, man of Kurkanza(?), for a person who has fallen ill 'through Išḫara' (a goddess of oaths) and died. The first column lists the goods prepared for the dead: garments, a chair and table, silver, gold, bronze daggers and cups, oil, honey, dried fruit, grain and breads; after a large break come lines of Hurrian incantation, the carrying out and burning of the dead, and a closing rite at dawn. The colophon names the scribe Angulli, son of Palla, working under Anuwanza.

paras.en: Thus (speaks) Zelliya, man of Kurkanza(?): If a person falls ill through Išḫara, and he …s (išḫarišḫari, i.e. suffers the Išḫara-illness?) and then dies — and his LÚMUSSAŠU (husband?) had been invited to bread (and) beer for him(?) — then afterwards I do as follows for the dead (person). I take these (things):

two white garments; two pairs of linen shirts (GÚ.È.A); one chair; one wicker table; one white kureššar-cloth; one shekel of silver; one shekel of gold; two bronze daggers; … cloth(?); two bronze cups; one NAMMANDU-vessel of oil; one NAMMANDU-vessel of honey; one handful of raisins; one handful of LAM.ḪAL-nuts; two baskets full of grain — of these, one basket full of emmer, [one basket] full of barley; one tarpala- (sash?) of red wool; one tarpa[la- …]; two kišri- (of wool); sixty thick loaves of one handful (each), [… thick loaves] of three handfuls; one kugulla- of beer-bread; ten ve[ssels …]; one pot of stew; one vessel of water of purification; for […]. All this I prepare, and […] after(wards?) … died(?), and this ritual for […] as follows: […]

When (it is) evening time […] I draw (water?) […]; when […] I place […] I place … […] one ta[ble …] for […] [break] Afterwards […] and the silver […] the gods of … […] [break] […] and … […] [Hurrian incantation, not understood: '… aruri … tārri (fire?) … ḫutmenanni … urunnina…']
And when [I …] these wo[rds], I car[ry] the dead one (GIDIM) outside, and I burn him up.
On the next morning, to the deity […]; but the words (are) exactly these […] is taken up(?) (karaptari), and he comes (back). Finished.
Hand of Angulli, the scribe, son of Pall[a]; in the presence of Anuwanza, the scribe of the house of […]. [About four lines left blank down to the lower edge.]
